4622579548.desc:
A 2027 wall calendar built from real sky data: a star chart for every month, the Moon for every night, and the eclipses and major meteor showers marked.
No shipping. Instant download. 4 PDFs: US Letter and A4, each in a dark Night and a white Ink-saver version.

WHAT IS ON EACH PAGE
- A round star chart of the sky overhead at 9 pm on the 15th, from 40° N (the latitude of New York, Philadelphia and Denver). Stars, constellation figures, and the planets that are up that night, placed where they will actually be.
- A short list of the month's events: eclipses, meteor shower peaks with the Moon's brightness that night, planet oppositions and close pairings, Mercury and Venus at their best, equinoxes and solstices.
- A month grid with a small Moon in every day box showing its shape that night, and the time of each new, first quarter, full and last quarter Moon. Plenty of room to write.

2027 HIGHLIGHTS ON THE CALENDAR
- Feb 6: annular solar eclipse (South America and the South Atlantic)
- Feb 10 and Feb 19: Jupiter and Mars at opposition, nine days apart
- Aug 2: total solar eclipse, up to 6 min 23 s of totality near Luxor, Egypt (path across Spain, North Africa and Arabia)
- Aug 12-13: Perseids · Dec 13-15: Geminids
- Oct 17: Saturn at opposition · Nov 24: Venus and Mars 0.3° apart in the evening sky
- Three penumbral lunar eclipses (Feb 20, Jul 18, Aug 17)

HOW THE DATES WERE MADE
Sun, Moon and planet positions are computed from NASA JPL's DE440 ephemeris. Every Moon phase was checked against the U.S. Naval Observatory, every planet event against the National Astronomical Observatory of Japan's 2027 almanac, the eclipses against NASA's eclipse catalogue (Fred Espenak), and meteor shower peaks come from the International Meteor Organization's 2027 calendar. Stars are from the Yale Bright Star Catalogue. Sources are listed on the last page.

TIMES
All times are U.S. Eastern Time (EST/EDT). The last page has a one-line conversion for Central, Mountain, Pacific, Alaska, Hawaii, Arizona, the UK and Central Europe. Moon phases happen at the same moment worldwide, so only the clock time changes; near midnight a date can shift by one.

- US Letter, Ink-saver version: white pages, dark stars
- A4 (210 x 297 mm), Night version
